text:
mila: quick heads-up — hitting an odd interop bug between python/node SDKs for embeddings+rerank in the sampleapp. looks like ordering + duplicate vectors when auth refresh triggers a retry. repro below.

andrew: hmm can you paste the minimal repro and the mismatched responses?

mila: repro steps: use embed batch helper with batch_size=3 on an 8-item payload, force token refresh (short-lived creds). python sdk call: `client.embeddings.create(inputs=batch)` -> returns `{"embeddings": [[...], [...], ...]}`. node sdk call: `client.embeddings({input: batch})` -> returns `[[...],[...],...]`. ordering is sometimes permuted on the node side after a 401->retry cycle. occasionally we get duplicate vectors for item 4 and missing vector for item 7.

sarah: that smells like the retry wrapper re-slicing the original buffer and then the batch helper re-queues items — double-batching. saw similar once when refresh produced a 401 and our retry enqueued the same sub-batch again.

leo: can you paste the exact log lines? also which SDK versions? we added a tiny reorder fix in the batching helper last quarter so might be related.

mila: logs (redacted):
```
[2026-03-22T15:02:17Z] embeddings: send batch id=0 items=3
[2026-03-22T15:02:17Z] auth: refresh token -> 401, refresh_started
[2026-03-22T15:02:18Z] embeddings: retry batch id=0 items=3 (from queue index 3)
[2026-03-22T15:02:18Z] embeddings: send batch id=1 items=3
[2026-03-22T15:02:19Z] response: embeddings returned 6 vectors for 6 inputs
[2026-03-22T15:02:19Z] final: output length mismatch expected=8 got=7
```

andrew: thanks. version?

mila: python sdk 0.9.3, node sdk 0.11.0. sampleapp pinned to python. node sampleapp uses `batchingHelper.enqueue` from @redwood/sdk-client.

sarah: probable root cause: the retry path reconstructs the batch from indices, but the batching helper expects to maintain a stable index map. if the helper is mutated after the retry starts you get dupes/missing. fix options: (1) make retry snapshot the exact item ids and payloads (deep copy) before sending, (2) make helper idempotent on re-enqueue, or (3) fix auth hook to block until refresh done.

leo: +1 for snapshotting in the short term. long-term we should ensure both SDKs share the same contract (always return `embeddings` key and stable ordering matching input order). that parity gap hurts DX.

mila: I made a tiny patch that deep-copies the sub-batch before send in node helper — seems to stop duplicates in local canary. PR: https://github.com/redwoodinc/redwood-sdk/pull/2489 (WIP).

andrew: great — can you add a regression test in the sampleapp that simulates a 401 during send and asserts ordering/length?

mila: yup added a mocha test and a deterministic auth-mock. linking in PR.

sdk-ci-bot: canary build queued for branch mila/emb-snapshot — build 4521.

sarah: also add a tiny shim in python SDK to normalize responses: if top-level is list, wrap into `{"embeddings": list}` so user code sees consistent shape across languages. keeps older clients working while we converge.

leo: will add an SDK-parity checklist item: embedding response shape + ordering guarantees + retry snapshot. drop-in tasks for docs too (onboarding note).

andrew: assign an owner and add to release notes. this is one of those sneaky DX bugs that surfaces as onboarding friction.

mila: owner is me, I'll update sampleapp, tests, and the PR today. thanks y'all :seedling: 

leo: once PR lands we'll run a dedicated e2e on dedicated infra (simulate token rotation) and then push the fix to canary.

mila: tl;dr — cause: retry + mutable batch helper -> reorder/duplicate; mitigation: snapshot before send + python response normalizer; next: parity test & docs.
